requirements.quote: Position: bit 2 of the Connect Flags.
requirements.condition: For the Will Flag in a CONNECT packet
requirements.required_behavior: Encode the Will Flag in bit 2 of the Connect Flags.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not encode the Will Flag in another Connect Flags bit.
requirements.why_checkable: The CONNECT flags byte can be masked at bit 2 and compared with the parsed Will Flag.

requirements.quote: If the Will Flag is set to 1 this indicates that, if the Connect request is accepted, a Will Message MUST be stored on the Server and associated with the Network Connection. The Will Message MUST be published when the Network Connection is subsequently closed unless the Will Message has been deleted by the Server on receipt of a DISCONNECT Packet [MQTT-3.1.2-8].
requirements.condition: When the Will Flag is 1 and the Server accepts the CONNECT request
requirements.required_behavior: Store a Will Message on the Server.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not accept the connection without storing the Will Message.
requirements.why_checkable: After an accepted CONNECT, Server session state can be inspected for a stored Will Message.

requirements.quote: If the Will Flag is set to 1 this indicates that, if the Connect request is accepted, a Will Message MUST be stored on the Server and associated with the Network Connection. The Will Message MUST be published when the Network Connection is subsequently closed unless the Will Message has been deleted by the Server on receipt of a DISCONNECT Packet [MQTT-3.1.2-8].
requirements.condition: When the Will Flag is 1 and the Server accepts the CONNECT request
requirements.required_behavior: Associate the stored Will Message with that Network Connection.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not associate the Will Message only with an unrelated connection.
requirements.why_checkable: Opening multiple connections and closing one can verify that the Will belongs to the correct connection.

requirements.quote: If the Will Flag is set to 1 this indicates that, if the Connect request is accepted, a Will Message MUST be stored on the Server and associated with the Network Connection. The Will Message MUST be published when the Network Connection is subsequently closed unless the Will Message has been deleted by the Server on receipt of a DISCONNECT Packet [MQTT-3.1.2-8].
requirements.condition: When a Network Connection with an associated Will Message closes and the Server has not deleted the Will after receiving DISCONNECT
requirements.required_behavior: Publish the associated Will Message.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not silently discard an undeleted Will Message when the connection closes.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can close the connection without DISCONNECT and observe whether the Will publication occurs.

requirements.quote:
Situations in which the Will Message is published include, but are not limited to:
An I/O error or network failure detected by the Server.
The Client fails to communicate within the Keep Alive time.
The Client closes the Network Connection without first sending a DISCONNECT Packet.
The Server closes the Network Connection because of a protocol error.
requirements.condition: When the Server detects an I/O error for a connection that has an associated Will
requirements.required_behavior: Publish the Will Message.
requirements.why_checkable: An injected I/O failure can be followed by observation of the Will publication.

requirements.quote:
Situations in which the Will Message is published include, but are not limited to:
An I/O error or network failure detected by the Server.
The Client fails to communicate within the Keep Alive time.
The Client closes the Network Connection without first sending a DISCONNECT Packet.
The Server closes the Network Connection because of a protocol error.
requirements.condition: When the Server detects a network failure for a connection that has an associated Will
requirements.required_behavior: Publish the Will Message.
requirements.why_checkable: An injected network failure can be followed by observation of the Will publication.

requirements.quote:
Situations in which the Will Message is published include, but are not limited to:
An I/O error or network failure detected by the Server.
The Client fails to communicate within the Keep Alive time.
The Client closes the Network Connection without first sending a DISCONNECT Packet.
The Server closes the Network Connection because of a protocol error.
requirements.condition: When a Client with an associated Will fails to communicate within the Keep Alive time
requirements.required_behavior: Publish the Will Message.
requirements.why_checkable: A timed test can suppress Client traffic and observe the resulting Will publication.

requirements.quote:
Situations in which the Will Message is published include, but are not limited to:
An I/O error or network failure detected by the Server.
The Client fails to communicate within the Keep Alive time.
The Client closes the Network Connection without first sending a DISCONNECT Packet.
The Server closes the Network Connection because of a protocol error.
requirements.condition: When a Client with an associated Will closes the Network Connection without first sending DISCONNECT
requirements.required_behavior: Publish the Will Message.
requirements.why_checkable: An abrupt Client close can be distinguished from a DISCONNECT and the Will publication observed.

requirements.quote:
Situations in which the Will Message is published include, but are not limited to:
An I/O error or network failure detected by the Server.
The Client fails to communicate within the Keep Alive time.
The Client closes the Network Connection without first sending a DISCONNECT Packet.
The Server closes the Network Connection because of a protocol error.
requirements.condition: When the Server closes a connection with an associated Will because of a protocol error
requirements.required_behavior: Publish the Will Message.
requirements.why_checkable: A protocol error can be injected and the subsequent Will publication observed.

requirements.quote: If the Will Flag is set to 1, the Will QoS and Will Retain fields in the Connect Flags will be used by the Server, and the Will Topic and Will Message fields MUST be present in the payload [MQTT-3.1.2-9].
requirements.condition: When the Will Flag is 1
requirements.required_behavior: Use the Will QoS field to control publication of the Will Message.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not ignore the Will QoS field.
requirements.why_checkable: The QoS of an emitted Will can be compared with the received Will QoS field.

requirements.quote: If the Will Flag is set to 1, the Will QoS and Will Retain fields in the Connect Flags will be used by the Server, and the Will Topic and Will Message fields MUST be present in the payload [MQTT-3.1.2-9].
requirements.condition: When the Will Flag is 1
requirements.required_behavior: Use the Will Retain field to control publication of the Will Message.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not ignore the Will Retain field.
requirements.why_checkable: The retained status of an emitted Will can be compared with the received Will Retain field.

requirements.quote: If the Will Flag is set to 1, the Will QoS and Will Retain fields in the Connect Flags will be used by the Server, and the Will Topic and Will Message fields MUST be present in the payload [MQTT-3.1.2-9].
requirements.condition: When the Will Flag is 1
requirements.required_behavior: Include the Will Topic field in the CONNECT payload.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: A CONNECT payload without Will Topic is forbidden under this condition.
requirements.why_checkable: The CONNECT payload can be parsed and checked for the field.

requirements.quote: If the Will Flag is set to 1, the Will QoS and Will Retain fields in the Connect Flags will be used by the Server, and the Will Topic and Will Message fields MUST be present in the payload [MQTT-3.1.2-9].
requirements.condition: When the Will Flag is 1
requirements.required_behavior: Include the Will Message field in the CONNECT payload.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: A CONNECT payload without Will Message is forbidden under this condition.
requirements.why_checkable: The CONNECT payload can be parsed and checked for the field.

requirements.quote: The Will Message MUST be removed from the stored Session state in the Server once it has been published or the Server has received a DISCONNECT packet from the Client [MQTT-3.1.2-10].
requirements.condition: Once the Server has published a Will Message
requirements.required_behavior: Remove that Will Message from stored Session state.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not retain the published Will in stored Session state.
requirements.why_checkable: Server session state or a subsequent reconnect/close can reveal whether the Will remained stored.

requirements.quote: The Will Message MUST be removed from the stored Session state in the Server once it has been published or the Server has received a DISCONNECT packet from the Client [MQTT-3.1.2-10].
requirements.condition: When the Server receives a DISCONNECT packet from the Client
requirements.required_behavior: Remove the connection's Will Message from stored Session state.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not retain that Will after DISCONNECT.
requirements.why_checkable: A graceful DISCONNECT followed by session inspection or reconnection can verify removal.

requirements.quote: If the Will Flag is set to 0 the Will QoS and Will Retain fields in the Connect Flags MUST be set to zero and the Will Topic and Will Message fields MUST NOT be present in the payload [MQTT-3.1.2-11].
requirements.condition: When the Will Flag is 0
requirements.required_behavior: Set Will QoS to 0.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not encode a nonzero Will QoS.
requirements.why_checkable: The Connect Flags byte can be masked at the Will QoS bits.

requirements.quote: If the Will Flag is set to 0 the Will QoS and Will Retain fields in the Connect Flags MUST be set to zero and the Will Topic and Will Message fields MUST NOT be present in the payload [MQTT-3.1.2-11].
requirements.condition: When the Will Flag is 0
requirements.required_behavior: Set Will Retain to 0.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not encode Will Retain as 1.
requirements.why_checkable: The Connect Flags byte can be checked at the Will Retain bit.

requirements.quote: If the Will Flag is set to 0 the Will QoS and Will Retain fields in the Connect Flags MUST be set to zero and the Will Topic and Will Message fields MUST NOT be present in the payload [MQTT-3.1.2-11].
requirements.condition: When the Will Flag is 0
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The Will Topic field MUST NOT be present in the CONNECT payload.
requirements.why_checkable: The payload field sequence can be parsed and checked for absence of Will Topic.

requirements.quote: If the Will Flag is set to 0 the Will QoS and Will Retain fields in the Connect Flags MUST be set to zero and the Will Topic and Will Message fields MUST NOT be present in the payload [MQTT-3.1.2-11].
requirements.condition: When the Will Flag is 0
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The Will Message field MUST NOT be present in the CONNECT payload.
requirements.why_checkable: The payload field sequence can be parsed and checked for absence of Will Message.

requirements.quote: If the Will Flag is set to 0, a Will Message MUST NOT be published when this Network Connection ends [MQTT-3.1.2-12].
requirements.condition: When a Network Connection whose CONNECT Will Flag was 0 ends
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The Server MUST NOT publish a Will Message for that connection.
requirements.why_checkable: Ending the connection and monitoring publications can verify that no Will is emitted.

requirements.quote: The Server SHOULD publish Will Messages promptly. In the case of a Server shutdown or failure the server MAY defer publication of Will Messages until a subsequent restart. If this happens there might be a delay between the time the server experienced failure and a Will Message being published.
requirements.condition: When the Server must publish a Will Message
requirements.required_behavior: Publish the Will Message promptly.
requirements.why_checkable: The term “promptly” supplies no measurable deadline, so the behavior cannot be judged consistently from this evidence.

requirements.quote: The Server SHOULD publish Will Messages promptly. In the case of a Server shutdown or failure the server MAY defer publication of Will Messages until a subsequent restart. If this happens there might be a delay between the time the server experienced failure and a Will Message being published.
requirements.condition: When a Server shutdown or failure occurs before pending Will Messages are published
requirements.required_behavior: The Server is permitted to defer those publications until a later restart.
requirements.why_checkable: MAY grants an optional behavior but imposes no mandatory observable choice or deadline for implementations that do not defer.

requirements.quote: Position: bits 4 and 3 of the Connect Flags.
requirements.condition: For the Will QoS field in a CONNECT packet
requirements.required_behavior: Encode Will QoS in bits 4 and 3 of the Connect Flags.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not encode Will QoS outside bits 4 and 3.
requirements.why_checkable: The Connect Flags byte can be masked with 0x18 and compared with the parsed Will QoS.

requirements.quote: These two bits specify the QoS level to be used when publishing the Will Message.
requirements.condition: When the Server publishes a Will Message
requirements.required_behavior: Use the two-bit Will QoS field as the Will publication QoS.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not select a different QoS independently of the Will QoS field.
requirements.why_checkable: The emitted PUBLISH QoS can be compared with the Will QoS supplied in CONNECT.

requirements.quote: If the Will Flag is set to 0, then the Will QoS MUST be set to 0 (0x00) [MQTT-3.1.2-13].
requirements.condition: When the Will Flag is 0
requirements.required_behavior: Set Will QoS to 0 (0x00).
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not encode Will QoS as 1, 2, or 3.
requirements.why_checkable: The two Will QoS bits can be checked for the fixed value 00.

requirements.quote: If the Will Flag is set to 1, the value of Will QoS can be 0 (0x00), 1 (0x01), or 2 (0x02). It MUST NOT be 3 (0x03) [MQTT-3.1.2-14].
requirements.condition: When the Will Flag is 1
requirements.required_behavior: Encode Will QoS as one of 0 (0x00), 1 (0x01), or 2 (0x02).
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not encode a value outside the listed Will QoS enumeration.
requirements.why_checkable: The two-bit field can be decoded and compared with the allowed set {0,1,2}.

requirements.quote: If the Will Flag is set to 1, the value of Will QoS can be 0 (0x00), 1 (0x01), or 2 (0x02). It MUST NOT be 3 (0x03) [MQTT-3.1.2-14].
requirements.condition: When the Will Flag is 1
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Will QoS MUST NOT be 3 (0x03).
requirements.why_checkable: The two Will QoS bits can be checked directly for the forbidden pattern 11.

requirements.quote: Position: bit 5 of the Connect Flags.
requirements.condition: For the Will Retain flag in a CONNECT packet
requirements.required_behavior: Encode Will Retain in bit 5 of the Connect Flags.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not encode Will Retain in another bit.
requirements.why_checkable: Bit 5 of the Connect Flags byte can be masked and compared with the parsed flag.

requirements.quote: This bit specifies if the Will Message is to be Retained when it is published.
requirements.condition: When interpreting the Will Retain bit
requirements.required_behavior: Use it to determine whether the Will Message is published as retained.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not interpret the bit as an unrelated flag.
requirements.why_checkable: The retained property of an emitted Will can be compared with this bit.

requirements.quote: If the Will Flag is set to 0, then the Will Retain Flag MUST be set to 0 [MQTT-3.1.2-15].
requirements.condition: When the Will Flag is 0
requirements.required_behavior: Set Will Retain to 0.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not set Will Retain to 1.
requirements.why_checkable: Bit 5 of the Connect Flags byte is directly testable.

requirements.quote: If Will Retain is set to 0, the Server MUST publish the Will Message as a non-retained message [MQTT-3.1.2-16].
requirements.condition: When the Will Flag is 1 and Will Retain is 0
requirements.required_behavior: Publish the Will Message as non-retained.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not publish the Will as a retained message.
requirements.why_checkable: A subscriber can inspect the RETAIN behavior of the Will publication.

requirements.quote: If Will Retain is set to 1, the Server MUST publish the Will Message as a retained message [MQTT-3.1.2-17].
requirements.condition: When the Will Flag is 1 and Will Retain is 1
requirements.required_behavior: Publish the Will Message as retained.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not publish the Will as non-retained.
requirements.why_checkable: A later subscription can verify that the Will was retained.

requirements.quote: Position: bit 7 of the Connect Flags.
requirements.condition: For the User Name Flag in a CONNECT packet
requirements.required_behavior: Encode the User Name Flag in bit 7 of the Connect Flags.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not encode it in another bit.
requirements.why_checkable: Bit 7 of the Connect Flags byte can be masked and compared with payload presence.

requirements.quote: If the User Name Flag is set to 0, a user name MUST NOT be present in the payload [MQTT-3.1.2-18].
requirements.condition: When the User Name Flag is 0
requirements.forbidden_behavior: A user name MUST NOT be present in the CONNECT payload.
requirements.why_checkable: The payload can be parsed and checked for absence of the user-name field.

requirements.quote: If the User Name Flag is set to 1, a user name MUST be present in the payload [MQTT-3.1.2-19].
requirements.condition: When the User Name Flag is 1
requirements.required_behavior: Include a user name in the CONNECT payload.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: A missing user-name field is forbidden.
requirements.why_checkable: The payload can be parsed and checked for presence of the user-name field.

requirements.quote: Position: bit 6 of the Connect Flags byte.
requirements.condition: For the Password Flag in a CONNECT packet
requirements.required_behavior: Encode the Password Flag in bit 6 of the Connect Flags byte.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not encode it in another bit.
requirements.why_checkable: Bit 6 of the Connect Flags byte can be masked and compared with payload presence.

requirements.quote: If the Password Flag is set to 0, a password MUST NOT be present in the payload [MQTT-3.1.2-20].
requirements.condition: When the Password Flag is 0
requirements.forbidden_behavior: A password MUST NOT be present in the CONNECT payload.
requirements.why_checkable: The payload can be parsed and checked for absence of the password field.

requirements.quote: If the Password Flag is set to 1, a password MUST be present in the payload [MQTT-3.1.2-21].
requirements.condition: When the Password Flag is 1
requirements.required_behavior: Include a password in the CONNECT payload.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: A missing password field is forbidden.
requirements.why_checkable: The payload can be parsed and checked for presence of the password field.

requirements.quote: If the User Name Flag is set to 0, the Password Flag MUST be set to 0 [MQTT-3.1.2-22].
requirements.condition: When the User Name Flag is 0
requirements.required_behavior: Set the Password Flag to 0.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The flag combination User Name=0 and Password=1 is forbidden.
requirements.why_checkable: Bits 7 and 6 can be checked for the prohibited combination 01.

requirements.quote:
Figure 3.5 Keep Alive bytes
Bit	7	6	5	4	3	2	1	0
byte 9	Keep Alive MSB
byte 10	Keep Alive LSB
requirements.condition: For the Keep Alive field in CONNECT
requirements.required_behavior: Place the most significant byte at byte 9.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not place the least significant byte at byte 9.
requirements.why_checkable: Byte 9 can be compared with the high eight bits of the decoded value.

requirements.quote:
Figure 3.5 Keep Alive bytes
Bit	7	6	5	4	3	2	1	0
byte 9	Keep Alive MSB
byte 10	Keep Alive LSB
requirements.condition: For the Keep Alive field in CONNECT
requirements.required_behavior: Place the least significant byte at byte 10.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not place the most significant byte at byte 10.
requirements.why_checkable: Byte 10 can be compared with the low eight bits of the decoded value.

requirements.quote:
Figure 3.5 Keep Alive bytes
Bit	7	6	5	4	3	2	1	0
byte 9	Keep Alive MSB
byte 10	Keep Alive LSB
requirements.condition: When encoding the two-byte Keep Alive field
requirements.required_behavior: Use most-significant-byte-first byte order.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not encode the field in little-endian order.
requirements.why_checkable: The consecutive MSB and LSB labels establish a directly testable big-endian ordering.

requirements.quote: The Keep Alive is a time interval measured in seconds. Expressed as a 16-bit word, it is the maximum time interval that is permitted to elapse between the point at which the Client finishes transmitting one Control Packet and the point it starts sending the next. It is the responsibility of the Client to ensure that the interval between Control Packets being sent does not exceed the Keep Alive value. In the absence of sending any other Control Packets, the Client MUST send a PINGREQ Packet [MQTT-3.1.2-23].
requirements.condition: When interpreting the Keep Alive field
requirements.required_behavior: Treat its numeric unit as seconds.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not interpret the value in another time unit.
requirements.why_checkable: Known field values can be tested against measured protocol timing in seconds.

requirements.quote: The Keep Alive is a time interval measured in seconds. Expressed as a 16-bit word, it is the maximum time interval that is permitted to elapse between the point at which the Client finishes transmitting one Control Packet and the point it starts sending the next. It is the responsibility of the Client to ensure that the interval between Control Packets being sent does not exceed the Keep Alive value. In the absence of sending any other Control Packets, the Client MUST send a PINGREQ Packet [MQTT-3.1.2-23].
requirements.condition: When encoding or decoding Keep Alive
requirements.required_behavior: Represent it as a 16-bit word.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not use a wider or narrower on-wire field.
requirements.why_checkable: The field width is directly inspectable as two bytes.

requirements.quote: The Keep Alive is a time interval measured in seconds. Expressed as a 16-bit word, it is the maximum time interval that is permitted to elapse between the point at which the Client finishes transmitting one Control Packet and the point it starts sending the next. It is the responsibility of the Client to ensure that the interval between Control Packets being sent does not exceed the Keep Alive value. In the absence of sending any other Control Packets, the Client MUST send a PINGREQ Packet [MQTT-3.1.2-23].
requirements.condition: For the unsigned 16-bit Keep Alive field
requirements.required_behavior: Use a value in the range 0 through 65535 seconds.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not encode a value greater than 65535.
requirements.why_checkable: A 16-bit unsigned on-wire word has the directly testable range 0..2^16-1.

requirements.quote: The Keep Alive is a time interval measured in seconds. Expressed as a 16-bit word, it is the maximum time interval that is permitted to elapse between the point at which the Client finishes transmitting one Control Packet and the point it starts sending the next. It is the responsibility of the Client to ensure that the interval between Control Packets being sent does not exceed the Keep Alive value. In the absence of sending any other Control Packets, the Client MUST send a PINGREQ Packet [MQTT-3.1.2-23].
requirements.condition: When measuring the Client's Keep Alive interval
requirements.required_behavior: Measure from completion of transmitting one Control Packet to the start of transmitting the next Control Packet.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not measure using different packet-boundary events.
requirements.why_checkable: Packet transmission timestamps expose both specified boundary events.

requirements.quote: The Keep Alive is a time interval measured in seconds. Expressed as a 16-bit word, it is the maximum time interval that is permitted to elapse between the point at which the Client finishes transmitting one Control Packet and the point it starts sending the next. It is the responsibility of the Client to ensure that the interval between Control Packets being sent does not exceed the Keep Alive value. In the absence of sending any other Control Packets, the Client MUST send a PINGREQ Packet [MQTT-3.1.2-23].
requirements.condition: While nonzero Keep Alive is enabled
requirements.required_behavior: Ensure the interval from finishing one Control Packet to starting the next does not exceed the Keep Alive value.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The Client must not remain silent beyond the Keep Alive interval.
requirements.why_checkable: A timed Client trace can compare consecutive packet-boundary timestamps with the negotiated value.

requirements.quote: The Keep Alive is a time interval measured in seconds. Expressed as a 16-bit word, it is the maximum time interval that is permitted to elapse between the point at which the Client finishes transmitting one Control Packet and the point it starts sending the next. It is the responsibility of the Client to ensure that the interval between Control Packets being sent does not exceed the Keep Alive value. In the absence of sending any other Control Packets, the Client MUST send a PINGREQ Packet [MQTT-3.1.2-23].
requirements.condition: While nonzero Keep Alive is enabled and the Client has no other Control Packet to send before the interval expires
requirements.required_behavior: Send a PINGREQ Packet within the Keep Alive interval.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not let the interval expire without sending either another Control Packet or PINGREQ.
requirements.why_checkable: A timed trace with no application traffic can verify the presence and deadline of PINGREQ.

requirements.quote: The Client can send PINGREQ at any time, irrespective of the Keep Alive value, and use the PINGRESP to determine that the network and the Server are working.
requirements.condition: At any time, regardless of Keep Alive
requirements.required_behavior: The Client is permitted to send PINGREQ.
requirements.why_checkable: This permission imposes no mandatory observable action and therefore cannot independently distinguish conformance.

requirements.quote: If the Keep Alive value is non-zero and the Server does not receive a Control Packet from the Client within one and a half times the Keep Alive time period, it MUST disconnect the Network Connection to the Client as if the network had failed [MQTT-3.1.2-24].
requirements.condition: When Keep Alive is nonzero and the Server receives no Client Control Packet within 1.5 times that period
requirements.error_behavior: The Server MUST disconnect the Client's Network Connection and handle it as a network failure.
requirements.why_checkable: A timed silent Client test can observe connection termination immediately after the specified threshold.

requirements.quote: If a Client does not receive a PINGRESP Packet within a reasonable amount of time after it has sent a PINGREQ, it SHOULD close the Network Connection to the Server.
requirements.condition: When a Client does not receive PINGRESP within a reasonable time after PINGREQ
requirements.required_behavior: Close the Network Connection to the Server.
requirements.why_checkable: The phrase “reasonable amount of time” provides no measurable threshold, so this excerpt does not define a deterministic conformance test.

requirements.quote: A Keep Alive value of zero (0) has the effect of turning off the keep alive mechanism. This means that, in this case, the Server is not required to disconnect the Client on the grounds of inactivity.
requirements.condition: When Keep Alive is 0
requirements.required_behavior: Disable the protocol's keep-alive timeout requirement.
requirements.why_checkable: The text removes a Server obligation but does not require either continued connection or disconnection, so no unique observable outcome is mandated.

requirements.quote: Note that a Server is permitted to disconnect a Client that it determines to be inactive or non-responsive at any time, regardless of the Keep Alive value provided by that Client.
requirements.condition: When the Server determines that a Client is inactive or non-responsive
requirements.required_behavior: The Server is permitted to disconnect the Client regardless of its Keep Alive value.
requirements.why_checkable: This is an unconditional permission rather than a required or forbidden behavior, so it cannot independently distinguish conformance.
